offer.say: Three songs and the dirge, dear. That's all I ask of it. But the batteries give up in the third and the dirge comes out like a sad cow. The referee thinks I'm being extra passive-aggressive. I'm being exactly as passive-aggressive as usual.

options.text: I'll find you a power adapter.
Why not just buy a new keyboard?
Maybe the sad cow is working.

new.say: A new one wouldn't know the songs. Organ 2 has been learning them since 1991. It's not a keyboard, it's a colleague.

options.text: A colleague needs power. I'll sort it.

cheek.say: Ha! Well, the Kessler bench did look upset. But I like to choose when I upset Kessler. It's my one hobby, besides piano.

decline.say: I bring eight. Pete buys them in bulk at Penner's. The keyboard eats them like crullers.

accepted.say: Try Bev. Bev keeps everything that isn't hers in a drawer. She says it's so people can come and get it. Nobody comes and gets it.

p_game.say: If the referee misses an offside I'll be at full volume. He's been warned.

complete.say: Full power, all three periods. The dirge was crisp. The ref looked right at me. I smiled. Now, you've earned a request. What shall Organ 2 play next game?

options.text: The Skaters' Waltz, during the intermission flood.
The dirge, for Kessler, every time they ice it.

c_waltz.say: For Doris. Earl will pretend not to like it. He'll slow down for the last chorus. He always does.

c_dirge.say: Every icing! Oh, I like you. Pete says I'm not to encourage you. I'm going to encourage you.

c_surprise.say: Organ 2 has a cha-cha setting nobody's heard since 1998. Brace yourself.
